summary: This resolution directs the House Fine Arts Board to accept a statue of Charlie Kirk by January 2, 2027, and display it permanently in a prominent location in the House wing of the Capitol.

scores.thoughts: The bill is a non-binding resolution directing the acceptance and display of a statue in the Capitol. It contains no provisions related to appropriations, budgets, or government expenditures of any kind.
The bill makes no reference to taxes, tax policy, rates, or revenue measures.
The bill is purely symbolic and contains nothing related to healthcare policy, coverage, or markets.
No provisions or references to firearms, regulations, or gun rights appear in the bill.
The bill does not address immigration, borders, or related policies.
No content in the bill pertains to abortion access or restrictions.
The resolution has no connection to military or defense spending.
The bill contains no environmental or regulatory provisions.
No references to welfare programs or social safety net policies exist in the text.
The preamble mentions Turning Point USA's educational mission, but the operative text is limited to statue placement and does not engage education policy.
The bill has no bearing on drug enforcement or decriminalization.
While the preamble notes Kirk's assassination, the bill itself proposes no criminal justice reforms or policies.
No trade, tariffs, or globalization provisions are present.
The bill does not address deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.
The resolution contains no provisions related to LGBTQ+ legal protections.
No foreign aid or international assistance measures are mentioned.
The bill does not engage with voting access, election integrity, or related reforms.
No technology, data privacy, or regulatory oversight provisions appear.
The bill has no connection to labor policy, unions, or worker protections.
The preamble references faith and constitutional rights, but the bill is symbolic and does not alter religious liberty or anti-discrimination policy.
